title: CareVista Hospitals to open 400-bed hospital in Visakhapatnam with a central laboratory
body: CareVista Hospitals will open a 400-bed multi-specialty hospital in Visakhapatnam in the second quarter of 2027, taking its network past 7,200 beds. The new hospital will include a central laboratory serving its Andhra Pradesh units, a 64-slice CT, a 3T MRI and a dedicated transplant wing. CareVista said procurement for laboratory automation, haematology and immunoassay analyzers will be run centrally from Hyderabad, with vendor evaluations starting in October. The group reported a 14 per cent rise in inpatient admissions last year and said the new hospital will also host a nursing college and a regional training centre for laboratory technicians.

title: MediNova Diagnostic Labs doubles reference laboratory capacity in Mumbai
body: MediNova Diagnostic Labs is doubling the capacity of its Mumbai reference laboratory to 40,000 samples a day and adding a molecular diagnostics floor for oncology and infectious disease panels. The expansion follows a 30 per cent rise in B2B testing volumes from hospitals. MediNova said it is evaluating a total laboratory automation track, additional clinical chemistry analyzers and a next-generation sequencing platform, and plans to place orders before the end of the financial year. MediNova operates 380 collection centres across Maharashtra and Goa, and said turnaround time for specialised tests has become a key factor for hospitals choosing a laboratory partner.

title: OnkoCare Cancer Centres plans three new cancer hospitals and an in-house pathology network
body: OnkoCare Cancer Centres will add three comprehensive cancer hospitals in Coimbatore, Madurai and Kochi over the next two years, with 150 beds each. The group is also building an in-house pathology and molecular laboratory network so that biopsy and tumour marker testing no longer needs to be outsourced. OnkoCare said it has budgeted for immunohistochemistry stainers, flow cytometry and digital pathology scanners, and will seek NABL accreditation for each laboratory. The group treats about 18,000 new cancer patients a year, and said faster in-house diagnosis should shorten the time between first consultation and the start of treatment by several days.

title: TrueLine Pathology Network raises Series B to open 12 regional labs in North India
body: TrueLine Pathology Network has raised INR 280 crore in a Series B round to open 12 regional laboratories and 250 collection centres across Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Haryana. Each regional lab will run haematology, biochemistry and immunoassay testing, with a hub in Lucknow for specialised tests. TrueLine said it will standardise analyzers across the network and is inviting proposals for reagent rental agreements and a cloud laboratory information system. The company currently processes about 9,000 samples a day across its existing laboratories, and expects volumes to more than double as the new regional network comes online next year.

title: Shreyas Hospitals commissions 300-bed hospital in Nashik, begins lab equipment procurement
body: Shreyas Hospitals will commission a 300-bed tertiary care hospital in Nashik in March 2027 with an investment of INR 520 crore. The facility will have 60 ICU beds, a cardiac cath lab and a 24x7 emergency laboratory. The hospital group has floated a tender for fully automated biochemistry and immunoassay analyzers, blood gas analyzers and a blood bank, and expects to award contracts by December so that equipment can be installed and validated before opening. Shreyas already operates four hospitals in Pune and Aurangabad, and said the Nashik hospital will serve patients who currently travel to Mumbai for complex cardiac and neurosurgical care.

title: Ayushman Medicity secures NABH accreditation, plans 200 additional beds in Jaipur
body: Ayushman Medicity has received NABH accreditation for its flagship hospital in Jaipur and will add 200 beds, including a 40-bed critical care block, by late 2027. The hospital said the accreditation audit highlighted the need to modernise its laboratory, and it will replace legacy semi-automated analyzers with integrated clinical chemistry and immunoassay systems. It is also planning a point-of-care testing programme for the emergency department and ICUs. The hospital handles about 2,500 outpatient visits a day, and said the laboratory modernisation will also support a new preventive health check programme aimed at corporate employees.

title: Genomix Bharat raises USD 22 million to build a high-throughput genomics lab in Bengaluru
body: Genomix Bharat, a preventive genomics start-up, has raised USD 22 million in a Series A round to build a high-throughput sequencing laboratory in Bengaluru capable of processing 5,000 genomes a month. The company offers hereditary cancer and cardiac risk panels through hospital partnerships. Genomix said the funding will go towards sequencers, automated liquid handling, sample storage and bioinformatics infrastructure, with equipment orders expected in the next two quarters. The founders said hospital partners in six cities have already signed up to refer patients, and that the company plans to publish population-scale genetic data in collaboration with universities.

title: Himadri State Medical Services Corporation tenders analyzers for 40 district hospital labs
body: The Himadri State Medical Services Corporation has issued a tender for the supply, installation and five-year maintenance of fully automated biochemistry analyzers, haematology cell counters and electrolyte analyzers for 40 district and sub-district hospital laboratories. The tender, valued at about INR 145 crore, also covers reagents on a cost-per-test basis. Bids close on October 20, and the corporation said preference will be given to vendors with service centres in the state. The corporation said the tender is part of a wider plan to offer free essential diagnostics at every district hospital, and a second tender for rural health centres will follow next year.

title: Sehat Diagnostics acquires 45 labs in Madhya Pradesh, plans network-wide automation
body: Sehat Diagnostics has acquired a network of 45 independent laboratories in Madhya Pradesh for an undisclosed sum, making it the largest diagnostics chain in the state. The company plans to consolidate testing into three hub laboratories in Bhopal, Indore and Jabalpur, each with pre-analytical automation and integrated chemistry and immunoassay lines. Sehat said it wants to complete the automation roll-out within 12 months and is in talks with equipment makers for bundled reagent contracts. The acquired laboratories together processed about 11,000 samples a day last year, and Sehat said it will retain the local brands while moving them onto a common technology platform.

title: Ganga Heart Institute to build a 180-bed cardiac hospital in Patna
body: Ganga Heart Institute will build a 180-bed cardiac hospital in Patna with two cath labs, a hybrid operating theatre and a round-the-clock cardiac biomarker laboratory. The project is funded through INR 310 crore of promoter equity and a term loan. The institute said it will run a single procurement for laboratory equipment, including troponin point-of-care analyzers and coagulation systems, and aims to open the hospital by the monsoon of 2027. Bihar has one of the lowest numbers of cardiac beds per capita in the country, and the institute said it has already recruited a team of interventional cardiologists for the new hospital.

title: Oasis Medical City expands laboratory and adds 250 beds in Abu Dhabi
body: Oasis Medical City will add 250 beds and a new central laboratory at its Abu Dhabi campus under a USD 180 million expansion plan. The laboratory will be fully automated and designed to meet CAP accreditation, with capacity for 25,000 tests a day serving the hospital and three satellite clinics. The hospital's procurement team said it expects to shortlist vendors for laboratory automation, microbiology and molecular platforms by the first quarter of next year. The hospital said patient volumes have risen by about a fifth over two years, and the expansion will allow it to bring back specialised tests that are currently sent to overseas reference labs.

title: Pranam HomeCare launches home diagnostics service across 15 cities after funding round
body: Pranam HomeCare has launched a home sample collection and diagnostics service in 15 cities after raising INR 90 crore from healthcare investors. The company will set up four processing laboratories to handle up to 8,000 samples a day and offer a subscription plan for chronic disease monitoring. Pranam said it is buying mid-throughput chemistry and HbA1c analyzers and is evaluating cold-chain sample transport boxes and a laboratory information system that integrates with its app. The company already serves 120,000 registered patients through its app and says repeat testing for diabetes and thyroid conditions makes up more than half of its current business.
